appearance_facts.location: May bar, rightmost position on the x-axis
appearance_facts.fact: The May bar is the shortest bar on the chart by a large margin; its top aligns with roughly 8,000–8,500 kWh on the y-axis.
The Jun bar is the next shortest, with its top near 17,500 kWh.
The Feb bar reaches approximately 20,000 kWh.
The Mar bar reaches approximately 26,500–27,000 kWh.
The Apr bar reaches just under 30,000 kWh.
The Jan bar is the tallest, reaching the 40,000 kWh gridline.
All bars are the same dark red/maroon color with no data labels printed on the bars themselves.

printed_facts.fact: Month; labels in left-to-right order: Apr, Jan, Jun, Feb, Mar, May
May is the rightmost month label on the x-axis

public_definitions: Goal: Review the monthly energy dashboard and decide whether May should be handled as a standard low-output case or escalated as a critical low-output anomaly.
Routing criterion: Whether May should be handled as a standard low-output case or as a critical anomaly.
Options: Route May to standard low-output follow-up; Escalate May to critical low-output anomaly review; Send May to background monthly record filing.
uncertain: No explicit threshold or rule is printed on the chart distinguishing 'standard low-output' from 'critical low-output anomaly'; the decision relies on relative comparison of May's bar to the other months.
Exact numeric value for May is not printed; it is estimated from the y-axis scale.
